verses.text: “Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let’s meet together for judgment.

Who has raised up one from the east? Who called him to his foot in righteousness? He hands over nations to him, and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.
He pursues them, and passes by safely, Even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.
Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”
The islands have seen, and fear. The ends of the earth tremble. They approach, and come.
Everyone helps his neighbor. They say to their brothers, “Be strong!”

So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. He who smoothes with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good”; and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter.
“But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the offspring  of Abraham my friend,
You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;’
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be like nothing, and shall perish.
You will seek them, and won’t find them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as nothing, as a non-existent thing.
For I, Yahweh your God, will hold your right hand, saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid. I will help you.’
Don’t be afraid, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I will help you,” says Yahweh, “and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in Yahweh. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy seek water, and there is none. Their tongue fails for thirst. I, Yahweh, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I will set cypress trees, pine, and box trees together in the desert;
that they may see, know, consider, and understand together, that Yahweh’s hand has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Produce your cause,” says Yahweh. “Bring out your strong reasons,” says the King of Jacob.
“Let them announce, and declare to us what shall happen. Declare the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come.
Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and see it together.
Behold, you are of nothing, and your work is of nothing. He who chooses you is an abomination.
“I have raised up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name; and he shall come on rulers as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay.

Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know? And before, that we may say, ‘He is right?’ Surely, there is no one who declares. Surely, there is no one who shows. Surely, there is no one who hears your words.
I am the first to say to Zion, ‘Behold, look at them;’ and I will give one who brings good news to Jerusalem.
When I look, there is no man; even among them there is no counselor who, when I ask of them, can answer a word.
Behold, all of them, their deeds are vanity and nothing. Their molten images are wind and confusion.

footnotes.content: The Lord calls for silence—not the silence of indifference, but of readiness. He invites the nations to draw near and speak their case, as if saying, 'Come, let us settle this together.' There's a courage in this openness, a confidence that His righteousness will stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This speaks of Cyrus, the Persian king, yet the pattern rings true: God raises up leaders for His purposes, giving them power as an instrument of His will. We see here that even earthly dominion serves a higher hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice the mystery: he passes through unknown ways 'safely,' treading ground never before touched by his feet. God walks with His instruments through unfamiliar territory. We too are guided even when the path seems strange.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the beginning to the end, God is 'I am He'—constant, purposeful, the one who holds all generations. When everything feels confused or temporary, remember: the Lord who called forth the first light is still here, still working.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations see and tremble. When God acts, creation responds. But notice what follows: they approach and come—not just in fear, but drawn forward. True reverence pulls us toward Him, not away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the face of God's power, what do the nations do? They help their neighbors, calling out, 'Be strong!' Even idolaters, it seems, know enough to encourage one another. How much more should we who know the Lord?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This describes the crafting of idols—carpenter and goldsmith at work, hammering and soldering to make their gods stable. But a god made by human hands, fastened with nails so it won't totter, reveals its own smallness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the Lord turns from the nations to His own: 'Israel, my servant.' The word 'friend' for Abraham is so tender—not just ancestor, but intimate companion. We inherit that same closeness when we belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the ends of the earth He called Israel; from the corners, He summoned them. And the word that followed: 'You are my servant. I have chosen you and not cast you away.' Once chosen, never abandoned—that is the covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five promises stacked like stones: 'I am with you. I am your God. I will strengthen. I will help. I will uphold.' Not vague comfort but specific pledges. When fear creeps in, remember: not one of these promises has been withdrawn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who rage against God's people will find their fury backfires. They are incensed, confounded, brought to nothing. This isn't vengeance spoken with malice, but a steady word: righteousness will outlast rage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will search for your enemies and find them gone—not because they won their fight, but because they have become as nothing. The Lord doesn't just defeat them; He removes them from the board entirely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord takes your right hand—the hand you work with, the hand you defend yourself with. He takes it not to constrain but to steady you. 'Don't be afraid,' He whispers. 'I will help.' His grip is certain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jacob is called a 'worm'—small, lowly, easily overlooked. Yet the Lord is their Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel. Never let weakness shame you: the smaller we see ourselves, the greater His mercy shines.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From worm to harvester: the Lord makes Jacob sharp, with teeth ready to thresh mountains down to dust. This is transformation—not escape from hardship, but strength to crush what stood against him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chaff is winnowed away. Rejoicing and glory follow—not before the work, but after it. When we have labored and seen the Lord's hand upon us, then joy rises unbidden, like spring after winter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The poor cry out with thirst, their tongue failing. But the Lord—'I will answer them.' He hears the voiceless, the forsaken. His response is not delay or distance but immediate attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On the bare heights, rivers open. In the valleys, springs burst forth. The wilderness becomes a pool. This is no timid restoration but a lavish reversal—thirst becomes abundance, barrenness blooms.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cedar, acacia, myrtle, oil trees, cypress, pine, box—the trees spread across waste ground. Each one planted by His hand. This is a gardener's work, deliberate and generous, healing the land itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All this flourishing—the waters, the trees—has one purpose: 'that they may see, know, consider, and understand' that Yahweh's hand did it. Creation itself becomes testimony to His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God invites the idols to present their case, to bring forth their 'strong reasons.' It's almost playful in its confidence—as if He's giving them every chance to prove themselves, knowing they cannot.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The test is clear: Can you declare what shall happen? Can you know the latter end of things? Only one who holds tomorrow can speak it truly. The idols are mute; only the living God knows what comes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do good or do evil—show us something, anything! But the idols have no power even to choose harm. They are paralyzed, unable to act. The contrast could not be sharper with the God who shapes nations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You are of nothing, and your work is nothing. Those who choose wooden gods choose what cannot last, what was never truly alive. It's a hard word, but spoken in hope—that Israel might turn and choose instead the God of all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again, Cyrus is raised from the north and east, calling on God's name. He shall come on rulers as on mortar, as the potter treads clay. The conqueror is in God's hand, an instrument of His justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who declared from the beginning what is coming? Who can say, 'He is right'? The silence answers itself: no one but the Lord. The idols have no voice to claim foresight, no word to prove themselves true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I am the first to say to Zion, 'Look!' The Lord brings good news to Jerusalem Himself. Not through intermediaries or slow rumor, but straight from His lips comes the gospel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When I look, there is no man, no counselor who can answer. The nations offer nothing of value, no wisdom for the crisis. Only the Lord Himself can speak what must be done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: all human achievement apart from God, all our vaunted works and images, are vanity and wind. Yet we still chase them. May the Lord keep turning us back to what alone endures—His kingdom and His steadfast love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
